questions.question: The ratio of speeds of A and B is 3 : 5. If A takes 24 minutes more than B to cover a certain distance, then how much time (in minutes) will B take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

Time taken by A to cover a distance = 24 minutes more than B 

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance traveled/Time taken

If Distance → Constant, then Speed ∝ 1/time

**Calculation:**

Ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

⇒ Ratio of time of A and B = 5 : 3

Let time taken by A and B be 5x and 3x respectively.

Difference in time taken by A and B = 5x – 3x = 2x = 24 mins.

⇒ x = 12

Time taken by B to cover the same distance = 3x = 3 × 12 = 36 mins

questions.question: The average number of students (per year), enrolled in B during 2015, 2016 and 2018 is more by what percentage than the number of students enrolled in A during 2017?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The average number of students enrolled in B during 2015, 2016, and 2018

⇒ (360 + 375 + 225)/3 = 320

The number of students enrolled in A during 2017 = 250

Required percentage = (320 – 250)/250 × 100 = 28%

questions.question: The total number of students enrolled in A during 2014, 2016 and 2018 is what percentage (correct to one decimal place) of the total number of students enrolled in B during the period of five years?
questions.solution:

The total number of students enrolled in B during the period of five years

⇒ 225 + 360 + 375 + 325 + 225 = 1510

Required percentage = 720/1510 × 100 = 47.7%

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 7, then x³ + 1/x³ is equal to:

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = a³ - 3a

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 73 - (3 × 7) = 322

**Detailed Solution:**

x + 1/x = 7

⇒ (x + 1/x)³ = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3(x + 1/x) = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3(7) = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 343 – 21

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 322

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 29282 in 4 years at 10% per annum, when the interest is compounded annually. What is the simple interest on the same sum for same time at the same rate?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount = Rs. 29282

Rate = 10% per annum

Time = 4 years

**Formula used:**

For compound interest,

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

For Simple Interest

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

Where, A = Amount

P = Principal

r = rate of interest

n = time period in years

**Calculation:**

⇒ 29282 = P(1 + 10/100)⁴

⇒ 29282 = P(11/10)⁴

⇒ P = 29282 × 10/11 × 10/11 × 10/11 × 10/11

⇒ P = Rs. 20000

Now,

S.I. = PRT/100

⇒ S.I. = (20000 × 10 × 4)/100

⇒ S.I. = Rs. 8000

By selling an article for Rs. 2300, Rekha gains 25%. If she sells it for Rs. 1955, then her loss/gain percent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

S.P. of an article = Rs. 2300

Gain% = 25%

**Formula used:**

C.P. = (S.P. × 100)/(100 + gain%)

Loss % = (Loss/C.P.) × 100%

**Calculation:**

C.P. of article = 2300 × 100/(100 + 25) = Rs. 1840

If the article is sold for Rs.1955, profit = 1955 – 1840 = 115

∴ Gain percent = 115/1840 × 100 = 6.25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Gain% = 25% = 1/4 

Ratio of C.P. to S.P. = 4 : 5

⇒ 5 units = 2300

⇒ 4 units = (2300/5) × 4 = Rs. 1840

If S.P. = Rs.1955, then Profit = 1955 - 1840 = 115

∴ Gain percent = 115/1840 × 100 = 6.25%

questions.question: If ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = 9 : 16. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 9 cm, then QR is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ΔABC ~ ΔQPR 

Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = 9 : 16

**Concept used:**

If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of their areas will be equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

⇒ Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = AB²/PQ²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side ΔABC : Side ΔPQR = √9 : √16 = 3 : 4

ΔABC ~ ΔQPR

⇒ AC/QR = 3/4

⇒ 9/QR = 3/4

⇒ QR = 12 cm

questions.question:
A wire is in the shape of a rectangle whose sides are in the ratio 7 : 4. It was initially in the shape of a circle of radius, very nearly equal to 31.5 cm. The length of smaller side of the rectangle is:

Take π = 22/7
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of sides of rectangle = 7 : 4

Circumference of wire = 31.5 cm

**Formula used:**

Circumference of circle = 2πr

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b)

**Calculation:**

Circumference of circle = 2 × 22/7 × 31.5

⇒ 198 cm

Let the length and breadth of rectangle be 7x and 4x respectively

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 2(7x + 4x) = 22x

Now,

Circumference of circle = perimeter of rectangle (as the wire is same)

⇒ 198 = 22x

⇒ x = 9

∴ The length of smaller side = 4x = 4 × 9 = 36 cm

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 10 days, B and C together can do it in 15 days while C and A together can do it in 20 days. They work together for 8 days. C alone will complete the remaining work in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Total Work** (LCM of 10, 15, 20) = 60 units.

Combined efficiency 2(A+B+C) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 ⇒ A+B+C = 6.5 units/day.

Work done in 8 days = 6.5 × 8 = 52 units.

Remaining work = 60 − 52 = 8 units.

Efficiency of C = (A+B+C) − (A+B) = 6.5 − 6 = 0.5 units/day.

Time taken by C = 8 ÷ 0.5 = 16 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (A + B) takes 10 days, (B + C) takes 15 days, (C + A) takes 20 days.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken
 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 A + B 10 60 6 
 B + C 15 4 
 C + A 20 3 
⇒ Adding efficiencies: 2(A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 13 ÷ 2 = 6.5 units/day

⇒ Work completed by all three in 8 days = 6.5 × 8 = 52 units

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 52 = 8 units

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A+B+C) − Efficiency of (A+B) = 6.5 − 6 = 0.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of C = 8 ÷ 0.5 = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Property

When pairs are given (A+B, B+C, C+A), the sum of their efficiencies is always twice the total efficiency of A, B, and C combined.

Pipes and Cisterns

This logic applies to pipes filling a tank, where negative efficiency is used for outlet pipes (leaks).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual or their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: A man gets a discount of 30% and then 20% on his food bill. How much equivalent single discount does he get?
questions.solution:
Given:

The successive discount are 30% and 20%.

Formula used:

Equivalent single discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

Where,

X = First discount

Y = Second discount

**Calculation:**

Equivalent single discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

⇒ 30 + 20 – (30 × 20)/100

⇒ 50 – 6

⇒ 44%

**∴ Equivalent single discount is 44%.**

questions.question: If one of the angles of a triangle is 64°, then the angle between the bisectors of the other two interior angles is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **triangle** with **interior angle bisectors**, the angle between the bisectors of the other two angles is given by the formula:

**Required Angle = 90° + (Third Angle / 2)**

Given the third angle (A) = 64°.

⇒ Required Angle = 90° + (64° / 2)

⇒ 90° + 32° = 122°.

**∴ The correct answer is 122°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **ΔABC**, let **∠A = 64°**. The **bisectors** of **∠B** and **∠C** meet at point **I** (the **incenter**).

**Formula Used:**

1. **Angle Sum Property**: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

2. In **ΔBIC**, ∠BIC + ∠IBC + ∠ICB = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/439094ad5075aa5b3ddd3a6285780864c9b2c12a188d9925eda62fbacd3d704e.png] 

**Calculations:**

In **ΔABC**:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 64° + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠B + ∠C = 180° − 64° = 116°

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ (∠B / 2) + (∠C / 2) = 116° / 2 = 58°

In **ΔBIC**, where **I** is the intersection of bisectors:

⇒ ∠BIC + ∠IBC + ∠ICB = 180°

Since **BI** and **CI** are bisectors, **∠IBC = ∠B / 2** and **∠ICB = ∠C / 2**:

⇒ ∠BIC + (∠B / 2) + (∠C / 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠BIC + 58° = 180°

⇒ ∠BIC = 180° − 58° = 122°

**∴ The correct answer is 122°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incenter (I)

The point where all three **internal angle bisectors** of a triangle intersect. It is the center of the **incircle**.

External Bisector Angle

The angle between the **external bisectors** of two angles of a triangle is given by **90° − (A / 2)**.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the **interior angles** of any triangle is always equal to **180°**.

Excenter Angle

The angle formed by one **internal bisector** and one **external bisector** of the other two angles is **A / 2**.</p

questions.question: The price of a commodity is increased by 36% and the quantity purchased is decreased by 30%. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the amount spent on the commodity?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Increase % in price of commodity = 36%

Decrease in quantity = 30%

**Concept used:**

Expenditure = Price of commodity × Quantity

**Calculation:**

Let the price of a commodity be Rs. 100/unit and the quantity purchased be 10 units

⇒ Amount spent = 100 × 10 = Rs. 1000

Now the price increased by 36%

⇒ The new price will be Rs.136/unit

The quantity purchased decreases by 30%

The new quantity purchased will be 10 × (100 – 30)/100 = 7 units

⇒ The new expenditure = 136 × 7 = 952

Decrease in amount spent = 1000 – 952 = Rs. 48

∴ Required percentage = 48/1000 × 100 = 4.8%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 400. After allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price, a shopkeeper makes a profit of Rs. 32. His gain percent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

M.P. of an article = Rs. 400

Discount % = 20%

Profit = Rs. 32

**Formula used:**

S.P. = M.P. × (100 - Discount%)/100

Profit = S.P. - C.P.

Profit % = Profit/C.P. × 100

**Calculation:**

S.P = M.P. × 80/100

⇒ 400 × 80/100

⇒ Rs. 320

C.P. = S.P. – Profit

⇒ 320 – 32

⇒ Rs. 288

∴ Gain percentage = 32/288 × 100 = 11.11%
